STEP INTO THE MOST EXCITING SCHOOL IN ENGLAND
THE VERY LATEST NEWS, EVENTS AND ANNOUNCEMENTS
Hurtwood Students Achieve Phenomenal A Level Results
From Hurtwood to Guildhall to Shakespeare’s Globe
Jack Huston stars with Nicholas Cage in Prime's 'Spider-Noir'
Hurtwood Film Academy meets Oscar-winning filmmaker David Puttnam
The Hurtwood Album 2025 Released Today
DRIVEN BY A PASSION FOR CREATIVITY AND ACADEMIC EXCELLENCE
Hurtwood combines the best elements of the traditional boarding school system with the best elements of the modern sixth form college to create a wholly unique and individual establishment.
While breaking new ground educationally, it has retained traditional values and has created an inspirational but safe stepping-stone between school and university.
View our latest results
This is a school driven by a passion for creativity and a respect for academic rigour, a small school with a distinctive voice which is less formal and less institutional than traditional public schools.
Hurtwood prides itself on the warmth of its relationships and its ability to engage closely with the hopes and aspirations of each individual student.
NEW STUDENTS NEW CHALLENGES
The students who come to Hurtwood House have usually been happy and successful at their former school, but they are now ready for fresh challenges.
They have reached an age when they feel that the learning methods and the lifestyle that worked for them when they were younger are no longer going to be as effective for them in the sixth form. At Hurtwood, they discover an intellectual and social environment closer to that of a university.
They find a sixth form which offers them a wider range of subjects and more flexibility of choice; a sixth form which is exceptionally strong academically with an outstanding record of A-level results placing Hurtwood consistently in the top five of all the co-ed boarding schools in the country.
One of England's most successful and exciting public schools.
All the students find Hurtwood a particularly easy school to join from a social point of view, because half of the school is new every year. The new students all arrive together and do not face the problem of joining a community where friendships have already been established over a period of many years.
LEARNING TO MAKE THE RIGHT CHOICES
Learning to make the right choices in life is an essential part of personal development. So many large schools have impersonal systems which stifle students’ individuality, their initiative and their creativity, and seek to push them down well-trodden paths into established channels.
At Hurtwood, guided by caring and experienced teachers, and in a carefully supervised and supportive environment, students are given the room to express themselves and encouraged to challenge the predictable.
Challenge is an important part of what Hurtwood is all about. Students learn to cope with change, to discover themselves and to learn how to get the best out of themselves. It is through rising to these challenges that their characters and personalities are shaped and defined.
When you visit, you are likely to be struck by the maturity of Hurtwood students and by the fact that they are already moving forward in life as happy, well-rounded and self-confident young adults.

ENGLISH LITERATURE
Here is a subject that can, through the magic of words, make us happy or sad, provoke us to think about deep issues or simply keep us amused or intrigued.
You will be introduced to prose, poetry and drama. Students will become familiar with different styles and they will learn to understand literary conventions and how they influence writing over time.
How English istaught at Hurtwood
ETHOS AND AIMS
The Department believes whole-heartedly in the power of reading and discussion to extend and develop our understanding of ourselves as free-thinking human beings.
English is taught through a balance of close study and free-ranging discussion, which aims to be lively, challenging and enjoyable. This then gives students a firm academic foundation which will enable them to progress onto Higher Education and beyond. The subject centres on discursive debate, evaluating the arguments of others, and encouraging genuine autonomy of mind. Weekly essays, coursework and final exams ensure that the skills of rigorous written argument are firmly embedded in each student.
It was a bright cold day in April, and the clocks were striking thirteen
CURRICULUM
The Department follows the Edexcel English Literature A Level course, 20% of which is assessed through coursework in the second year, with the remaining 80% assessed in three examinations: Poetry, Drama and Prose.
In the A1 year, we study a range of Georgian and modern prose, theatre and poetry. This includes an anthology of modern poetry by the likes of Fanthorpe, Duffy and Armitage, novels by Shelley and Atwood, and a play by Tennessee Williams. These texts are all studied with an emphasis on close analysis of writer’s craft, encouraging enquiry into the mechanics of the interaction between structure, style and effects.
In the second year, we study a range of Early Modern and Medieval texts, as well as some more modern texts. These include Shakespeare, Chaucer and a two-text coursework comparison piece, with material varying according to individual teacher.
EXTRA-CURRICULAR
Students who wish to extend their passion for creative writing are encouraged to join ’Muse’, our platform for the creative student voice, which meets regularly across the year directed by Sam and Louise. Together, we produce collaborative work, creative and journalist pieces, enter original work for national competitions, as well as running a blog and a podcast.
We also have an Advanced English group which meets once a week to develop and extend the knowledge base of keen readers.
We offer an annual trip of literary significance – in previous years, this has included Dublin and Paris literary tours, an overnight stay in Stratford to see the RSC perform ‘Hamlet’, trips to live performances of texts, and talks from visiting practitioners from across the literary profession.

FRENCH
Bonjour et bienvenue à tous !
If you are contemplating taking French you have come to the right place. Find answers below to any questions you may have that can help you decide on taking the course.
ETHOS AND AIMS
The Department aims to develop and interest in and an enthusiasm for the French language, by teaching in a lively and communicative way, using the latest technologies, francophone songs and films.
It also aims to assist students to becoming independent learners by ensuring that they are actively involved in their learning and increasing their motivation and confidence. Students will develop understanding of the language in a variety of contexts and genres and communicate confidently, clearly and imaginatively in French.
A vaincre sans péril, on triomphe sans gloire
CURRICULUM
The French Department follows the Edexcel A Level course.
Students will develop their awareness and understanding aspects of the contemporary society, cultural background and heritage of a francophone country.
In the A1 year, students will concentrate on two themes: social issues and trends and artistic culture (through music, festivals and traditions) and political and artistic culture (through media). Students will develop their speaking, listening, reading and writing skills from a variety of authentic sources, covering different contexts, registers, styles and genres.
In the A2 year, students will focus on two other themes: immigration and the multicultural society in French and the period of the French Occupation and Resistance. In the course of the two years, students will be also studying in depth a film 'Les Choristes' by Christophe Barratier and a book 'No et Moi' by Delphine de Vigan.
EXTRA CURRICULAR
Students are encouraged to spend time in France.
Language trips can be organised on an individual basis or in groups in a language school in Nice for one week to 2 months, during the holiday. Students can immerse themselves in the culture and practise the language by going to lessons in the morning and on excursions in the afternoons.

MUSIC TECHNOLOGY
Industry professionals abound and their experience brings a cutting edge to both the teaching and performing. Students are given every chance to explore their creative talents and are constantly challenged to improve in this dynamic environment.
How Music istaught at Hurtwood
EXTRA-CURRICULAR
There is a wide range of opportunities for musicians, songwriters and producers within the musical life of the school.
Instrument, Vocal and Songwriting Lessons
Instrument, vocal and songwriting lessons with practicing industry professionals are available to all students whatever standard from beginner to Grade 8 and beyond.
Students are encouraged to perform in the various shows and concerts, both formal and informal, which take place throughout the year. Own compositions are positively encouraged and supported by songwriting lessons and musicianship Enigma sessions. Music Technology students form an integral part of the technical team for the shows which initiates them into the dynamic world of live sound.
Album Academy - The Hurtwood Album
The Hurtwood Album is produced every year and students can be involved both as instrumentalists and engineer/producers. Again, Music Technology students take the lead in the production process and are encouraged to work well beyond the standards expected at A Level. The very best in the year are invited to join Album Academy where they learn advanced recording and production techniques and are ultimately responsible for delivering the Hurtwood Album. As with all Hurtwood endeavours, expectations are high and students work with industry professionals throughout.
WINNER – BEST EXPERIMENTAL LEARNING MUDDY STILETTOS
Project YouTube offers an incredible opportunity for students to showcase their talents to a global audience and receive recognition for their work. This initiative includes professional music video shoots, featured on a YouTube channel with tens of thousands of subscribers. Students from across the school are invited to participate, whether as singers, musicians, film crew, or photographers, in what has become an outstanding platform for creativity.
While auditions are held annually for singers, musicians have the chance to engage in various performance opportunities throughout the year. A dedicated crew of filmmakers, audio technicians and photographers also contributes to the success of each video project, ensuring a high standard of production.
Previous videos from Project YouTube have received millions of views, setting a benchmark for excellence. Many students involved have gone on to secure work in their chosen fields, making this project an ideal stepping stone for those looking to launch their careers.
If you’d like to see some of the videos produced by Project YouTube then please click here.
The Hurtwood Concert
This is one of the main events of the school year. The Hurtwood Concert is an immense high-octane mix of lights, projections, film, dance and sound. All types of music are represented from Classical to Jazz, Rock, and Pop, and previous years have also included Irish Folk, Opera and Traditional Chinese Music played on authentic instruments. This is your chance to perform with the support of a professional band supported by lights and sound designed and operated by industry professionals. The competition for concert slots is fierce but there are roles for everyone, and many students say this is the most rewarding thing they do at Hurtwood.
Step into a vibrant and welcoming atmosphere with our regular Lunchtime Concerts! These informal sessions give students the perfect opportunity to showcase their talents in a relaxed setting, performing to an enthusiastic and appreciative Hurtwood audience. Whether it's an intimate solo or a dynamic group performance, these concerts celebrate the diverse musical abilities of our students and are a popular way to brighten up the day with live music.
Get ready for the ultimate rock showdown! The "Gig of Glory" is our annual spectacle where school rock bands take centre stage, backed by full Hurtwood technical support. This high-energy event has quickly become one of the most anticipated highlights of the year, delivering unforgettable performances and raw musical talent. With a concert experience that rivals professional gigs, it’s a must-see event for anyone who loves live music and the excitement of rock 'n' roll.
The Classical Concert
Once a year, the stage is set for elegance and sophistication as we host the prestigious Classical Concert. This evening is dedicated to showcasing the exceptional classical music talent at Hurtwood, featuring stunning performances that highlight the grace, skill, and passion of our students. From orchestral pieces to solo performances, this concert is a true celebration of timeless music and artistry.
4 digitalrecordingstudios
CURRICULUM
The department follows the Edexcel A Level course which has elements of project work as well as assessment through final examinations.
Students produce a portfolio of 2 projects made up of a multitrack recording and a composition. These form 40% of the overall A level mark. All of the practical work is realised through technology and there is no instrument or vocal performance element in the assessment. The end of year examinations consist of a practical Analysing and Producing paper and a Listening and Analysing paper together forming the remaining 60% of the A level. Popular Music genres from the 1950s to present day are studied together with the history of the technology used to create them. Both of these exams contain questions on sequencing, performance and recording techniques as well as aspects of audio and electronics theory.
Photo: By JannikSet1 (Own work) [CC BY-SA 4.0 (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0)], via Wikimedia Commons
ETHOS AND AIMS
The delivery of Music Technology at Hurtwood is unlike anything available in other schools and offers a uniquely creative learning experience that leads to so much more than simply a good qualification.
Whilst academic success is fundamental, the Music Department strives to inspire our musicians, songwriters and producers by immersing them in the latest technology and exposing them to professional standards wherever possible. We hold true to our vision of being one of the best equipped departments in the country and look to facilitate creativity at all times. The four purpose built recording studios and the dedicated MIDI Suite boast Apple Mac computers running industry standard software including Pro Tools and Logic. The way music is created, performed and listened to has totally changed over the past few decades and it is vital that today’s musicians marry traditional skills and knowledge with an understanding of how to fully utilise the technology available to them. The department encourages creative excellence and offers numerous opportunities to work alongside industry professionals. This “real world” experience provides a unique creative edge to the academic work undertaken by our students. It is the aim of the department that at the end of their time at Hurtwood, our students will be well placed to pursue further study at University or to take up positions working in the industry. If you love performing or producing music then this is the course for you.
The music tech facilities here are amazing, I was blown away when I first walked into the recording studio

Drama
At Hurtwood we look to shock, amaze and challenge our students, not only through work within the course, but through exposure to a range of other theatre experiences and extra-curricular activities.
The successis builton passion
Extra-Curricular
We mount in-house productions to a high standard; we invite top experimental and fringe companies to perform and have co-produced Edinburgh Fringe productions.
We also run trips out to local and West End theatres. Our focus is not only on conventional theatre, for we believe in the integration of the arts, so dance, musical theatre and performance art all feed into the rich diet of the Theatre Studies student at Hurtwood. Students have the opportunity to learn from working professionals in a variety of different ways including workshops, masterclasses and one to one tuition. Extra-curricular projects include: The Hurtwood Musical, The Hurtwood Music Concert, Outdoor Shakespeare Project, Acting & Dance Companies, Musical Theatreshowcase, plus regular Lunchtime and Classical Concerts. Students can also develop backstage and design skills through working with our team of technical professionals who supportall of our extra-curricular productions.
Through the year we run a Musical Theatre course in the Enigma program for A1 students. Initially this introduces students to the ways song, dance and acting skills combine, but as the year goes on it focuses on rehearsal for an end of year Showcase. We combine a selection of numbers, linked together with a loose theme, in which all cast members have their moment to shine and present it in the last week of the summer term.
"A true masterclass in what school theatre can achieve when talent, ambition, and passion align." NATIONAL SCHOOL THEATRE AWARDS
WINNER – BEST MUSICAL NATIONAL SCHOOL THEATRE AWARDS
Straight Drama Productions
For A1 students, there is an Enigma option especially for those that are serious about straight drama. An auditioned ensemble of some of Hurtwood's finest A1 actors perform in the summer term at the local Cranleigh Arts Centre, directed by Ezra Hjalmarsson, one of our resident drama teachers and directors.
Students are encouraged to write and direct their own work and where possible this is showcased informally with all the full artistic and technical support that Hurtwood can offer.
Backstage/Technical Theatre
The technical support for our production is outstanding and the designers and operators we use are top notch. The equipment that we own and hire is state of the art and we have a dedicated team of full-time technicians providing support for all our productions. These work alongside the industry professionals we import to work on specific projects. Students regularly go on to study Stage Management and Technical Theatre at the top colleges, and we strive to make students realize that what happens behind the scenes is as important as what happens onstage.
Private Acting Classes
Students can take one to one acting skills sessions with peripatetic actors and directors who will work with them on developing their techniques. We also have extensive complimentary sessions to prepare students for drama school auditions including a showcase to perform their efforts to their peers alongside a selection of agents and casting directors invited from London.
Hurtwood Festival of Drama
In the spring we have a run of plays and monologues which are part of the Theatre Studies academic exams. Students work hard to put on their own productions which are open to the public and also assessed for their A Levels.
The Christmas Musical
This is not just any school play. Our aim is to take you on a journey which ends up as near as possible to a full on professional West End experience. It is something of an occasion, running for two weeks and attracting a large regular following which includes agents and casting directors.
This is a huge event involving up to one third of the school and a whopping big budget to support the show. Whether it's a classic like West Side Story or Guys & Dolls, a popular compilation show like All Shook Up or We Will Rock You, or one of our own devised adaptation like Cyrano, every show we present has a generous sprinkling of Hurtwood creative magic which brings an originality and excitement to the work. We see this as something you will want to remember for the rest of your life!
How TheatreStudies is taught atHurtwood
Curriculum
The Theatre department is responsible for preparing students for Edexcel A Level Drama and Theatre examinations.
We offer a two year A Level course working with a variety of theatre practitioners and professionals. Team-teaching and group work are at the heart of our success and we want students who work well in a team, have positive energy and are prepared to ‘have a go!’
Being creative and being brave are fundamental to our performance work at Hurtwood House and we can guarantee that the confidence and the skills that you acquire will be useful to you whatever direction you take next.
The Edexcel A Level course is divided into 3 Components:
Component 1: Devising - Students will devise an original performance worth 40% of the A Level
Component 2: Text in Performance - Students will be directed in a group production and present a monologue or duologue to a visiting examiner. This is worth 20% of the A Level.
Component 3: Theatre Makers in Practice - Students will evaluate live theatre and explore two set texts in preparation for a final written exam. This is worth 40% of the A Level.
Please click the Specifications link at bottom of page for more info.
ETHOS AND AIMS
The aim of the department is to run an integrated course, which involves team teaching, to produce work of high quality and originality and we insist that our students show respect for ourselves, for others and the work we do.
We encourage the necessary self-discipline required to be a member of a team: positive energy, focus and commitment, creativity and imagination, generosity and trust. We teach the skills of practical control and expertise, clear, confident and fluent vocal work, experimentation and daring and reflection and research. We aim to develop students who have a high level of dramatic and theatrical skill and understanding, who have encountered a broad range of theatrical experiences, have pride and ownership in what they do and who have made a significant personal journey through their time with us.
A week after my interview l heard that I had received a full scholarship.

SEE OUR STUDENT SUCCESSES
DRIVEN TO CREATE
The defining feature of Hurtwood is its creativity. “It is the glory of Hurtwood,” according to the Good Schools Guide, “and is at the heart of its ethos.” Hurtwood provides outstanding opportunities for the aspiring actor, singer, artist, fashion designer, dancer or filmmaker.
"There is a glittering array of performance opportunities – some related to the A-level Theatre Studies course, but many more available outside school hours, all run to professional standards, largely because the teachers are West End/Media pros, absolutely on top of their game jaw-droppingly good concerts and theatre shows." Good Schools Guide.
The Christmas musical, for example, is a £100k production with a cast of 70-80 students performing for ten nights with a full West End band and professional musical directors, choreographers and lighting designers. The same dynamic is applied to the Summer musical and to the February Rock & Pop concert – another £50k extravaganza featuring 20-30 students, many of whom have gone on to great things over the years – visit our Hall of Fame.
There is a wide variety of straight drama and improvisation built into the A-level course, with an exciting weekly programme of theatre skills including stage combat and circus skills. Outside that, our Drama Company runs a year-long, highly specialised “drama school” course, providing training to all students auditioning for the major drama, dance and music schools, and acting lessons for stage and screen.
DRAMA
WE’VE TAKEN DRAMA TO A STANDARD PREVIOUSLY THOUGHT UNACHIEVABLE
Hurtwood has the largest and most professional theatre department of any school in the country.
Over a dozen hands-on theatre practitioners challenge the students to work to professional standards in an atmosphere of creative collaboration.
Working with such seasoned professionals means high expectations and a demanding workload, but offers the opportunity to perform with the best at the very highest level.
The only school that taught me anything. And what they taught me completely shaped the outcome of my life HANS ZIMMER PAST STUDENT
MEDIA
Hurtwood provides a media education which is dynamic, provocative and rewarding – and unparalleled at this level.
With state-of-the-art technology and high levels of expertise and instruction, students are given the freedom to be creative and the tools to achieve at the highest level.
MUSIC
Hurtwood is awash with opportunities for the musically minded.
Elaborately staged concerts and musical showcases give artistes the opportunity to perform with professional musicians in front of audiences which often include agents and record companies. More than 100 of our students take music and singing lessons, and many a musical career has started here, whether it be on stage or in our state of the art recording studios.
DANCE
A passion? A hobby? A career?
Whether it is classical ballet, lyrical jazz, musical theatre, contemporary, tap, flamenco, pas de deux, modern, commecial hip-hop or Bollywood; whether it is for fitness or for fun; and whether it is curricular or extra-curricular, Hurtwood offers an extraordinarily rich and varied diet of dance styles and techniques.
ART
We have one of the most successful and exciting Art & Design, Textiles and Photography departments in the country.
Expectations are high. The atmosphere is stimulating and vibrant and students produce portfolios rich in their diversity and creativity and of extremely high quality.
TEXTILES
We believe that students can, through careful guidance and clear demonstrations, be taught a broad range of diverse textile techniques, including basic skills of drawing and observation.
We have high expectations of our students and this is reflected by the excellent examination results that have been achieved and the high percentage of students that gain access to Foundation and Degree courses in Art and Design both in the UK and abroad.
PHOTOGRAPHY
If a picture is worth a thousand words it could be argued that the camera has done more to shape our opinions, our tastes and our view of the world than any invention since the printing press.
Photography is now the most widespread form of image-making in the world. Newspapers and magazines and advertising hoardings feed us thousands of photographic images every day, and they are perhaps more influential than we care to admit.
DISCOVER OUR HALL OF FAME

LIFE AFTER HURTWOOD
SUCCESSFUL REALISATION
University, drama school, art school, film school – an outstanding record of placing students on the next stage of their careers.
With Hurtwood’s superb A level results it is not surprising that the vast majority of our students go on to degree courses at England’s top universities. The courses they take range from Astrophysics and Macro Biology to Economics and Psychology.
WHERE OUR STUDENTS GO
A DIVERSE RANGE OF DEGREES
Our academic graduates go on to study:
Academic Subjects – Medicine, Veterinary Science, Economics, History, Mathematics, Management, Psychology, Law, Engineering.
Our creative graduates go on to study:
Performing Arts – Acting, Dance, Musical Theatre
Creative Fields – Fashion, Fine Art, Film, Photography, Animation, Music Production, Music Performance
EXPERT UNIVERSITY AND CAREERS GUIDANCE
ANNUAL UNIVERSITY & CAREERS FAIR
ACADEMIC PATHWAYS
Careers and Higher Education Fair: Talks on different subjects and the opportunity to speak directly to admission tutors.
Professional advice: Hurtwood's experts provide individual help choosing university courses, completing applications and crafting the best personal statements.
Oxbridge: Intensive Oxbridge preparation with advice on choosing a college, preparation for entry tests, mock interviews and alumni talks.
Medicine and Veterinary science: Intensive Medical School and Veterinary Science preparation with alumni talks, advice on entry tests and mock interviews.
London: Imperial LSE King's UCL SOAS Queen Mary
Elsewhere in UK: Cambridge Oxford Durham Bath St Andrews Machester, Exeter Birmingham Bristol Edinburgh Newcastle Surrey Cardiff Warwick Loughborough Brighton and Sussex Medical School
From choosing a course, preparing my application, to finalising my choices, the Hurtwood Careers team supported me every step of the way. I am forever indebted for the guidance on my journey and encouragement along the way.
Zaria Jankelovitz-Gelvan
Reading English at Downing College, Cambridge in 2025
PERFORMING ARTS AND CREATIVE PATHWAYS
Film & Media: Talks from industry specialists and Hurtwood Film Academy prepare students for the film industry. Hands-on experience with 16mm film, live streaming and documentary filmmaking giving students the best portfolios and a head start at university
Drama School Preparation: Extensive help with choice and rehearsal of audition pieces.Weekly masterclasses with industry professionals such as Adrian Rawlins, Paul Bown, and Tom Mison.
Dance Training: Individual training from professionals in jazz, tap, modern, ballet, contemporary and street dance. Bespoke help with audition pieces and choreography.
Fine Art & Design: Art Masterclasses, Life Drawing Sessions, visits from professional artists, 1:1 portfolio guidance and visits from leading art Schools.
Music & Music Production: There are multitude of performance opportunities and experience in songwriting, recording and production with the Hurtwood album and Project YouTube which help students access the best courses.

I am so grateful for the constant support that Hurtwood gave me – there was always a Drama teacher available to help me with my auditions.
Joining NYU Tisch in 2025

ART
At Hurtwood House we encourage the individual to embrace art as a means of self-expression, freedom, life and imagination.
Art is the desire to create, to make send of the world and oneself. Since the dawn of civilization man has tried to capture the image of his surroundings and used a variety of media to accomplish this. Art is the communication of ideas, information and emotions, whether through drawing, painting or any other material that will leave a trace or a mark.
How Art is taughtat Hurtwood
CURRICULUM
The department follows the AQA A Level course in Art and Design with opportunities to specialise in Fine Art, Constructed Textiles and Photography.
Each of these subjects are assessed through a combination of examination and coursework. The diversity of the course makes it ideally suited for students intending to go on to Foundation Art and Design courses and Degree courses specialising in many aspects of Art such as Fine Art, Fashion, Textiles, Photography, Architecture, Product Design, Interior Design, Theatre and Costume Design, Art History, Graphics, Animation and Film. Students of Art and Design go on to a wide range of courses. There is also the option at many Universities to combine Art with other subjects in a modular degree programme. In the first year, students study how to develop their visual language through a carefully structured sequence of workshops. They create an extended project of their own choice building a portfolio and working towards producing a professional final outcome. In the second year, students study a range of more advanced concepts, in particular looking at the development of a personal investigation through whatever media they choose. This is celebrated in their end of year exhibition.
ETHOS AND AIMS
The main purpose of the Fine Art, Constructed Textiles and Photography courses is to develop the student’s ability to appreciate the visual world and to respond in a personal and creative way.
The Art department staff devise and implement projects which encourage students to question all pre-conceived notions of Art and personal ability. To trust their creative instincts and enjoy expressing their ideas and feelings through the controlled use of a broad range of techniques and materials. As well as investigating and relating to all the evolutionary processes that are inherent in the development of good design, students are encouraged to articulate issues relating to the work of other artists from a variety of cultures, past and present. The Art Studios are very much a centre of creativity and self-expression, and they have an “open house” policy that allows students to work there during activities afternoons and open studio weekends throughout the academic year.
Art Gallery
What is asketchbook?
It may seem strange to ask the question "what is a sketchbook?", because there are many different ideas about what the word means. The range of interpretations can be confusing and off-putting. Sketchbooks should be both enjoyable and serious. They require a degree of commitment from the beginner that may be quite daunting at first.
Trust your creative instincts
EXTRA-CURRICULAR
We arrange visits to Universities and Art colleges for the students so that they can view the Foundation Art shows and meet the staff who will talk to prospective applicants about their courses.
Each year about 90% of the students studying Art and Design decide to specialise in the subject at Art College. All of our students have been successful in gaining places at either Art College or University. Trips to the London galleries are also part of our curriculum delivery, these include Tate Modern, Tate Britain, The Victoria & Albert Museum, and The Design Museum. The Department also organises a 5 day residential trip to Venice, apart from the Architectural experience, this includes visits to the Penny Guggenheim Museum, Murano glass workshops and Contemporary Art galleries. In addition, students’ work is entered for a number of different national competitions, providing opportunities to attend presentations in locations such as the Saatchi Gallery.
The Enigma program offers a huge range of activities from wine tasting to a great range of sports. I hope to go on to complete an architectural degree.

GEOGRAPHY
Geography is about understanding the world. It illuminates the past, explains the present and prepares us for the future.
Without Geographyyou are nowhere!
ETHOS AND AIMS
The Geography department provides students with a unique opportunity to explore the human, physical and environmental interactions of our planet.
Geography is a dynamic discipline which seeks to explain physical landforms and phenomena along with giving us a clearer insight into how human activities are shaping the characteristics of our world. The course offers an exciting variety of content and also encourages students to develop a wide and valuable skills base. By studying Geography at Hurtwood, students will be engaged and informed about topical issues, as well as developing their capacity to understand our complex world. They will be challenged to discuss, debate and think geographically about the people and places of the 21st Century.
CURRICULUM
The department follows the OCR A level course. In the first year, we study both human and physical geography through the topical and influential themes of Disease Dilemmas, Coastal Landscapes, and Changing Spaces; Making Places. Throughout, students will consider their own values and attitudes and support their learning through examining real case studies. Within and beyond the classroom, students will also develop a variety of geographical skills, which will equip them with practical and transferable life skills. In the second year, we explore three key themes: Global Systems and Global Governance, Earth’s Life Support Systems, and our Hazardous Earth. Within these themes we consider global challenges and explore the ‘big’ questions concerning the future and sustainability of our planet. The course is examined through a variety of short answer, essay and enquiry-based written examination papers.
EXTRA CURRICULAR
Geography is the 'window on the world’ and as such it requires us to look out of the window.
An important element of the course is therefore our commitment to fieldwork and exploring real scenarios beyond the classroom. To support students’ geographical understanding and develop their examinable fieldwork skills, they will work as a team on various field activities. Day visits and local enquiries support learning and allow students to collect data in order to complete a personal fieldwork investigation worth 20% of the A Level award. Our recent trip to Iceland gave students the opportunity to experience first-hand the power and complexity of our planet. The department is a member of both the Royal Geographical Society and the Geographical Association and attends lectures and events to enrich students’ learning.

HISTORY
At Hurtwood we study both the 19th and 20th centuries, with a strong emphasis on the latter period and on a global view of events.
Students can relate more effectively to these time periods than, say, the medieval period. The philosophy behind teaching the Modern period is that all the students will have a far more informed perception of the world they live in and will be able to follow current affairs with far greater appreciation than those with only a shallow and Euro-centred knowledge of the present day.
How History istaught at Hurtwood
ETHOS AND AIMS
“The most effective way to destroy people is to deny and obliterate their own understanding of their history.” ― George Orwell
We aim to inspire an interest in, and love of, the past, so that pupils will continue to read and enjoy history throughout their adult lives.
The department teaches synoptically, building up the student’s understanding of some of the key forces which shaped the landscape of the twentieth century. This enables us, in A2 to forensically examine the history of Britain as an imperial power and an international influence from the 18th to the 20th centuries. This will provide a strong foundation for post Sixth Form study.
Hurtwood is a bridge between school and University study, and the Department is focused on providing our students with the skills to thrive at that next level. Overall, our courses provide pupils with a thorough understanding of the political, social, cultural and religious issues of the past, both through investigative learning and from the perspectives of contemporaries and historians.
A large number of pupils go on to study the subject at university in order to develop a career in Law, International relations, Finance, the Arts, and beyond.
CURRICULUM
The History department follows the EDEXCEL A Level course which is assessed both through examination and coursework.
In the A1 year, students study the impact of Communism on the Russian people. They will also study the development of China under the leadership of Chairman Mao.
In the A2 year, students study a range of more advanced concepts, in particular looking at the development of the United Kingdom as an international force. The study begins with the loss of the Thirteen Colonies which went on to become the bedrock of the United States of America; it goes on to conclude with Britain at its imperial peak on the eve of the Great War.
Students are required to complete one piece of coursework which accounts for 20% of the overall A Level grade. This is either an investigation into the impact that Stalin had upon the legacy of Lenin following the latter's death in 1924 or an explanation of the reasons that lead to the development of the Cold War 1945-1991.
Annual trips to stunning places inhistory.
EXTRA-CURRICULAR
The department offers an ‘Advanced History’ course on Friday afternoons, which looks to construct a breadth of understanding of history as a discipline and to encourage critical thinking.
As Jose Marti once said: “The first duty of a man is to think for himself”. As such, we offer classes in topics as diverse as ‘Athenian and Roman Democracy’, ‘Hobbes, Locke and Libertarianism’, ‘De Tocqueville: Democracy in America’, ‘Whig History’ and ‘Kant, Hegel and idealism in History’. Through this introduction to the development of human civilisation, its ideas, cultures, actions and beliefs, the Department aims to provide a basis for intellectual growth and the sharing of ideas.
The department runs an annual trip to the Portsmouth Historic Dockyard and on occasions attends conferences in London specifically geared to support our programme of study. We have also run trips to Moscow, St. Petersburg, Berlin and Cuba. Additionally, the department undertakes trips for the purposes of academic enrichment with a highly successfulvisit to Iceland looking at the history of the Vikings as the most recent example.
I’m doing PPE at Oxford, I could not have achieved that at any other school.

BIOLOGY
There is no better way to appreciate the complexities of evolution, the elaborate networks of ecology and Man’s effect on his surroundings than to immerse yourself in it in the way that only Hurtwood can.
How Biology is brought to life at Hurtwood House
ETHOS AND AIMS
The aim of the biology department is to develop the students biological knowledge in association with real life examples of biology at work.
To take account of some of the new advances in the field of biology and the issues these raise. Have an awareness of the application of biology in a variety of fields of study. To allow the students to develop the necessary skills to pursue a career in scientific study or to be able to transfer these skills to other areas.
Biologyis a ‘living’ science
CURRICULUM
Edexcel Biology A (Salters-Nuffield)
Topic 1: Lifestyle, Health and Risk
This looks at cardiovascular disease (CVD) and includes the circulatory system and the importance of lifestyle choices to health. The structures of some carbohydrates and lipids are also detailed within this context.
Topic 2: Genes and Health
This topic considers the following biological principles through the context of the genetic disease cystic fibrosis: the properties of and transport of materials, across cell membranes and gas exchange surfaces; DNA structure and replication; protein synthesis, enzymes and monohybrid inheritance.
Topic 3: Voice of the Genome
This looks at the development of multicellular organisms from single cells to complex individuals. Looking at cell structure and ultrastructure, cell division, fertilisation, stem cells, gene expression and cell differentiation. Also the role on the environment when considering the expression of the genotype and the influence of epigenetic changes.
Topic 4: Biodiversity and Natural Resources
Starting with species diversity and the concept of niche and adaption this topic looks at the wealth of natural resources available to and exploited by humans. This includes medicines and fibres and a consideration of how zoos and seedbanks can help in conservation.
Topic 5: On the Wild Side
Photosynthesis is the primary process that underpins the majority of ecosystems, being an important component of the carbon cycle. This topic looks at how climate change can influence species distribution and how the evidence for climate change has been collected.
Topic 6: Immunity, Infection and Forensics
What questions need to be answered when a body is found? This topic looks at the work of a forensic pathologist along with how bacteria and viruses may have cause the death in the first place. It also looks at the complexity of the immune response and how an evolutionary race exists between the pathogens and the human immune system.
Topic 7: Run for your life
Sports science is the context for this topic looking at respiration, muscle contraction and homeostasis. Including the use of performance enhancing drugs as well as the mechanisms available for monitoring performance.
Topic 8: Grey Matter
The scene is set by considering how the nervous system enables us to see. Brain imaging and the regions of the brain are considered as are how imbalances in brain chemicals may result in conditions such as Parkinson’s disease.
Practical work will be carried out throughout the course and a number of skills will be assessed.
EXTRA CURRICULAR
Field work – to include grass and fresh water ecology.
Dissection (not compulsory)

CHEMISTRY
Chemistry is the intriguing study of everything.
This A Level course starts you on a journey of knowledge, discovery and excitement that may lead you wherever your imagination will take you.
Chemistry is essential for other sciences
ETHOS AND AIMS
As a rigorous academic subject, chemistry is one of the most well-respected subjects to study at any level. It provides insights into the world we experience from the macroscopic to the nanoscale and beyond. Studying Chemistry at A Level will give you an essential understanding of the scientific method, the theory underpinning the nature of matter and it will develop your problem-solving skills. It is vital to your understanding of the key issues facing your generation: antibiotic resistance, development of fertilisers, renewable energy sources and drug development.
How Chemistryis taughtat Hurtwood
CURRICULUM
At Hurtwood, the AQA A-level Chemistry course is studied. This course is a two year linear course.
This course is a two-year linear course. Each year of the course is split into topics which cover a wide range of areas relating to the Organic, Inorganic and Physical fields of Chemistry. Students regularly undertake practical work to learn a wide variety of practical techniques over the two-year course.
For the full course specification, please click here
EXTRA CURRICULAR
The department offers weekly support sessions to help students achieve the best possible results.

REQUEST A PROSPECTUS
We would be delighted to send you a copy of our Hurtwood House prospectus. Please complete the request form below.
Please fill in this field.

MEDIA STUDIES
This is undoubtedly the most professional media set-up we have ever seen. Anywhere.
"Squillions of pounds and a wealth of experience on the teaching side. This is professional stuff. The media/theatre complex is huge; think masses of green rooms, mixing studios, dance studios, recording studios, video studios." THE GOOD SCHOOLS GUIDE
How Media Studiesis taught at Hurtwood
The Media department follows the CIE A Level Media Studies.
In the A1 year, students study how social representations are created in film and television texts and carry out case studies of the relationships between institutions and audiences in the UK and US film industries. They will also work towards the production of a film opening sequence for their coursework portfolio. In the A2 year, students study a range of more advanced concepts, such as the characteristics of postmodern media and the complexities of regulating content in the online era. They also complete a coursework portfolio, consisting of a range of products linked to a music industry marketing project.
Highest Mark inthe World for A Level Media2023 & 2024
Students with a particular interest and aptitude for filmmaking are encouraged to apply for the Hurtwood Film Academy, which offers a select group advanced training in fiction and documentary film production, undertaking a variety of film projects across the three-term course.
All Media students participate in an annual awards ceremony, in which student work is celebrated with a screening and awards distributed in a number of different categories. In addition, students’ work is entered for a number of different national competitions, providing opportunities to attend screenings and ceremonies in locations such as the National Film Theatre on the South Bank.
Film Academy
The Hurtwood Film Academy works as a production company within the school. Students train in all aspects of film and post production, working alongside professional filmmakers to turn their ideas into finished films. For a look at some of HFA's work, please click here.
ETHOS AND AIMS
The department aims to equip students for life outside of Hurtwood by developing their awareness of how different media influence or reflect our views of ourselves and society in a variety of ways.
Through building an understanding of the complex relationships between media products, their audiences and their institutional contexts, we study some of the key debates around the power of media texts. Our quality training of media production skills encourages students to learn how to express themselves as media producers in their own right.
View our YouTube channel
This channel contains a selection of projects produced by our A Level Media Studies students at Hurtwood House School.
This is undoubtedly the most professional set-up we have ever seen.
The teaching we have at this school is just incredible, the teachers aren't boring old duffers, they are industry professionals!

pageCache.pageTitle: From Hurtwood to Guildhall to Shakespeare’s Globe
pageCache.text:
From Hurtwood to Guildhall to Shakespeare’s Globe
Congratulations to ex-Hurtwood student Fia Hadeed who is making her stage debut in Shakespeare’s ‘Much Ado About Nothing’ at the Globe Theatre, directed by Chelsea Walker, as part of their Summer Season 2026.
After Hurtwood Fia went to study Acting at Guildhall School of Music and Drama. She graduated in 2025, but her television credits already include ‘Private Bushra Abdallah’ in Russell T Davies’ series ‘The War Between the Land and the Sea’ for BBC/Disney+ which premiered in 2025, and ‘Nour’ in ‘The Gathering’ for World Productions/Channel 4, which premiered in 2024.
At Hurtwood, Fia lit up the stage in many productions and concerts, but it was her performance as ‘The Witch’ in Hurtwood’s Christmas musical ‘Into The Woods’ which was the most memorable. She was also the lead singer in Hurtwood’s ‘Project YouTube’.
At the Globe, Fia will be acting alongside Bridgerton’s Geraldine Alexander, and we are sure that it won’t be long before Fia is a household name herself.

pageCache.pageTitle: Creative & Performing Arts A-Level Subjects - Hurtwood House
pageCache.text:
A UTOPIA FOR CREATIVE MINDS
DRIVEN TO CREATE
The defining feature of Hurtwood is its creativity. “It is the glory of Hurtwood,” according to the Good Schools Guide, “and is at the heart of its ethos.” Hurtwood provides outstanding opportunities for the aspiring actor, singer, artist, fashion designer, dancer or film maker.
There is a glittering array of performance opportunities, some related to the A-level Theatre Studies course, but many more available outside school hours, all run to professional standards, largely because the teachers are West End/Media pros, absolutely on top of their game jaw-droppingly good concerts and theatre shows.” Good Schools Guide.
The Christmas musical, for example – a £100,000 production with a cast of 70 or 80 students with the incredible opportunity of performing for 10 nights will full West End band, and professional musical directors and choreographers and lighting designers. The same dynamic is applied to the Summer musical and to the February rock and pop concert – another £50,000 extravaganza featuring 20 or 30 Hurtwood students, many of whom have gone on to great things over the years – see Hall of Fame.
There is a wide variety of straight drama and improvisation and an exciting weekly programme of theatre skills as various as stage combat and circus skills, built into the A-level course. Outside that, there is a year-long, highly specialised “drama school” course, run by our Drama Company, special training given to all students auditioning for the major drama, dance and music schools, and acting lessons for stage and screen.
DRAMA
WE’VE TAKEN DRAMA TO A STANDARD PREVIOUSLY THOUGHT UNACHIEVABLE
Hurtwood has the largest and most professional theatre department of any school in the country.
Over a dozen hands-on theatre practitioners challenge the students to work to professional standards in an atmosphere of creative collaboration.
Working with such seasoned professionals means high expectations and a demanding workload, but offers the opportunity to perform with the best at the very highest level.
The only school that taught me anything. And what they taught me completely shaped the outcome of my life HANS ZIMMER PAST STUDENT
MEDIA
Hurtwood provides a media education which is dynamic, provocative and rewarding – and unparalleled at this level.
With state-of-the-art technology and high levels of expertise and instruction, students are given the freedom to be creative and the tools to achieve at the highest level.
MUSIC
Hurtwood is awash with opportunities for the musically minded.
Elaborately staged concerts and musical showcases give artistes the opportunity to perform with professional musicians in front of audiences which often include agents and record companies. More than 100 of our students take music and singing lessons, and many a musical career has started here, whether it be on stage or in our state of the art recording studios.
DANCE
A passion? A hobby? A career?
Whether it is classical ballet, lyrical jazz, music theatre, contemporary, tap, flamenco, pas de deux, modern, commecial hip-hop or Bollywood; whether it is for fitness or for fun; and whether it is curricular or extra-curricular, Hurtwood offers an extraordinarily rich and varied diet of dance styles and techniques.
ART
We have one of the most successful and exciting Art & Design, Textiles and Photography departments in the country.
Expectations are high. The atmosphere is stimulating and vibrant and students produce portfolios rich in their diversity and creativity and of extremely high quality.
TEXTILES
We believe that students can, through careful guidance and clear demonstrations, be taught a broad range of diverse textile techniques, including basic skills of drawing and observation.
We have high expectations of our students and this is reflected by the excellent examination results that have been achieved and the high percentage of students that gain access to Foundation and Degree courses in Art and Design both in the UK and abroad.
PHOTOGRAPHY
If a picture is worth a thousand words it could be argued that the camera has done more to shape our opinions, our tastes and our view of the world than any invention since the printing press.
Photography is now the most widespread form of image-making in the world. Newspapers and magazines and advertising hoardings feed us thousands of photographic images every day, and they are perhaps more influential than we care to admit.
DISCOVER OUR HALL OF FAME

DANCE
Here at Hurtwood the dance department strive to develop dancers who are: creative, technically proficient, and exceptional performers who are also knowledgeable about the exhilarating world of dance. We have a busy, exciting and thriving department where dance can be studied at A Level as well as an extra-curricular activity for all levels. A variety of classes across a wide range of dance styles are held every day.
How Dance is taught at Hurtwood
EXTRA-CURRICULAR
The dance department at Hurtwood offers a vibrant and exciting choice of additional weekly technique classes which are open to all students. There is a great energy and buzz coming from the dance studio daily! These classes are wide-ranging from ballet, jazz, hip hop and commercial, to tap, lyrical, contemporary, and musical theatre. The Dance department also runs the prestigious Hurtwood Dance Company who train for 2 and a half hours every week to develop their technical and performance skills. Students must audition at the beginning of the year to gain a place, and as a result, feature highly in the Hurtwood concert and Dance showcase.
The Hurtwood Dance Company
For the experienced dancer the Dance Company is probably the most exciting opportunity at Hurtwood - an intensive two-year training programme for the school's most competent and committed dancers, exposing them to a professional level and pace, developing their stamina and technique and preparing them for dance colleges and for the business itself. A range of professional dancers and teachers from Dance Colleges around the UK visit the school to work with the students to help prepare them for auditions.
Extra-curricular Dance classes are currently offered in Jazz, Ballet, Contemporary and Tap. These classes are specifically catered to the student’s needs, and are streamed in levels of ability from complete beginners to the highly advanced.
Enigma Dance Options
Every week dance is offered in at least one of the Enigma options. Recent courses have included Street Dance, Come dancing - Latin and Ballroom, Bollywood Dance, Hip-Hop & Commercial Dance and Dance aerobics.
Hurtwood's three major yearly productions all have a strong emphasis on dance and choreography. Often working with outside professional choreographers, the shows are a great way to experience dance at Hurtwood and put the skills learnt in classes into practice. We also have a more informal summer term Dance Showcase for students to present work.
A Utopia forcreativeminds
CURRICULUM
The Department follows the AQA A Level course which is assessed both practically and through a written examination. Dance follows a linear programme where all assessment takes place at the end of the second year. The course is evenly split into 50% practical and 50% theory. For the practical component, students are given the opportunity to choreograph their own group dance - for this they effectively become the teacher! Students create on their peers, in response to an examination question set by the exam board during the second year of study. For technique and performance, students prepare two exam pieces. In the first of these pieces, candidates are required to dance a solo in the style of a choreographer, which links to the theoretical component of the course. For the second performance, students are required to dance as part of a quartet. These pieces are both prepared over the course of the two years. As part of technical training, all A1 students work towards Grade 6 Contemporary NATD exam which is taken at the end of the first year. This qualification counts for UCAS points and provides another qualification alongside the A Level.
The theoretical component is assessed through a written examination where students bring together their knowledge of the two areas of study. The compulsory area of study is Rambert Dance Company which is the UK’s leading and oldest contemporary dance company. The second area of study looks at the history of American Jazz from 1940-1975, focusing on key practitioners such as Jerome Robbins and Bob Fosse who contributed hugely to the development of the jazz genre. For each of these areas of study a range of practitioners and their works will be explored, with specific focus on the two set works; Rooster by Christopher Bruce and Singin in the Rain by Gene Kelly.
We recommend that all A Level dance students take advantage of the range of extra-curricular dance on offer here at Hurtwood. A Level dancers are expected to attend a supplementary technique class each week to help develop their technique and performance skills.
ETHOS AND AIMS
Through the A Level programme, we aim to develop the three fundamental areas of performing, choreographing, and appreciating dance. These skills are developed within a variety of theoretical and practical classes that take a holistic approach. We nurture our students through technique classes in contemporary, ballet and jazz, as well as choreographic and performance workshops. In theory classes students are introduced to a wide range of professional dance works and are welcomed to discuss the subject matter of these pieces, which often tackle issues relevant to society today.
